thread:
Maya (Finance): Heads up — we kicked off the Billmesh pilot today to test their invoice connector for usage reconciliation. Quick few questions about how they report API vs embedding lines.
Ashok (Procurement): Nice, do we have the pilot SOW? any spend cap?
Maya (Finance): SOW is attached in the drive: <https://drive.redwood.com/pilot-billmesh>. It lists a $5k pilot cap but unclear if overages are auto-billed.
Claire (EngOps): Pinged Sam from Billmesh in DM — their product maps tokens into two SKUs: generation.api and embed.v1. That mapping caused a duplicate line in our import.
InvoiceBot: Invoice import failed for file invoice_2026-03-23.csv — duplicate SKU mapping detected: generation.api vs generation_v1.
Sam - Billmesh: Sorry about that — our export includes legacy SKU aliases. For pilots we can collapse aliases to a single SKU (generation.api) and add a metadata column "pilot_account_id". Will push a corrected export by EOD.
Maya (Finance): Thanks Sam. Also need clarity on how monthly committed credits apply. Do credits apply first to generation tokens or to embeddings? Our usage profile is 70% generation, 30% embeddings.
Sam - Billmesh: Credits apply proportionally by invoice line by default. We can change to priority consumption (apply to embeddings first) if you want — but that requires a config flag and is a commercial term.
Ashok (Procurement): If changing consumption order is a commercial term, what's the negotiation leeway for a pilot? Can we get one-time credit for onboarding anomalies?
Sam - Billmesh: For pilot customers we typically offer a one-time migration credit up to 20% of pilot cap to cover mapping issues. We can add a clause to the pilot SOW.
Claire (EngOps): One more question: how do they compute usage windows? We saw a spike in token counts when several parallel requests hit the same cached prefixes; is Billmesh de-duping prefix cache hits or counting per-request tokens?
Sam - Billmesh: Billmesh measures tokens at the compute layer post-batching. So parallel requests that share KV cache still count tokens per response. We can provide a breakdown by request_id for auditing.
Maya (Finance): That helps. For our cost model we need a daily CSV with fields: date, sku, tokens, billable_units, pilot_account_id, invoice_credit_applied. Can you commit to that?
Sam - Billmesh: Yes — we can provide a daily export and a reconciliation report mapping your internal route ids to our usage rows.
Ashok (Procurement): On approvals — who signs the SOW? Finance needs a clause about "no automatic renewal after pilot" and procurement needs a PO ceiling rather than auto-billing.
Maya (Finance): Agreed. Add: "Pilot invoices require manual approval; no auto-renew or charge beyond $5,000 without written PO."
Sam - Billmesh: We can accept that for pilots. I'll add it to the SOW and send the updated doc.
Claire (EngOps): FYI — we'll run a synthetic load test tomorrow to validate token attribution. Please don't finalize mapping before we run it.
InvoiceBot: Reminder — updated import file uploaded by Sam at 2026-03-23T17:12:34Z: invoice_2026-03-23-v2.csv
Maya (Finance): Once we have the corrected export and the daily CSV schema, finance can sign-off on the pilot. Also want a quick billing contact in case we see overages — Sam, who should we ping?
Sam - Billmesh: Please ping me (sam@billmesh.com) and our billing lead, tanya@billmesh.com. We'll set up a shared Slack channel if helpful.
Ashok (Procurement): Can procurement get a CA/NDAs copy? we need legal review before the pilot goes live fully.
Maya (Finance): Added to the drive folder. Legal review requested; procurement will await their sign-off before any invoice is paid.
Claire (EngOps): I'll post test vectors and expected token counts in the thread after the load run.
Maya (Finance): Great — next steps: Sam to update SOW with manual-approval clause + migration credit; Billmesh to provide daily CSV; EngOps to run synthetic test and validate. I'll hold payment until reconciliation matches. :thumbsup:
